Darnassus: The night elf capital rests high in the boughs of Teldrassil, a World Tree grown without the dragon Aspects' blessing. From the Temple of the Moon, High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind leads her people and their Sentinels.
Ironforge: Carved deep into the mountains of Khaz Modan around the roaring Great Forge, the dwarven capital is ruled by King Magni Bronzebeard. Since Gnomeregan fell, its Tinker Town has sheltered the exiled gnomes as well.
Orgrimmar: Thrall raised this walled city in a red-rock canyon of Durotar and named it for Orgrim Doomhammer, the Warchief who freed him. It stands as the beating heart of the new Horde on Kalimdor.
Stormwind City: Rebuilt from the ashes of the First War, the human capital gleams with white stone. Yet the boy-king Anduin reigns in his missing father's place, and the masons who raised these walls were never paid.
Thunder Bluff: The tauren capital crowns a cluster of towering mesas above Mulgore, linked by rope bridges and reached by creaking lifts. High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof founded it once the Horde helped drive the centaur from tauren lands.
Undercity: Beneath the ruins of Lordaeron's capital lie the old royal crypts and catacombs, now a sprawling city of the Forsaken. Here the Banshee Queen, Sylvanas Windrunner, rules, and her Royal Apothecaries brew a new plague.
Blackfathom Deeps: Once a temple to Elune on the shores of Ashenvale, these flooded halls sank long ago. Now naga and the Twilight's Hammer cult lurk in the dark water, venerating the ancient beast Aku'mai.
Blackrock Depths: Within the bowels of Blackrock Mountain lies Shadowforge City of the Dark Iron dwarves. Emperor Dagran Thaurissan rules here, heir to the sorcerer whose summoning of Ragnaros scorched the land around it for good.
Blackrock Spire: The fortress at the top of Blackrock Mountain bristles with orcs of the Dark Horde under Warchief Rend Blackhand, while General Drakkisath and the black dragonflight guard its upper halls.
Dire Maul: The crumbling ruins of Eldre'Thalas, a Highborne city older than the Sundering, sprawl across the forests of Feralas. Gordok ogres squat in its courtyards while the last elves within feed on a captive demon's power.
Gnomeregan: The gnomes' wondrous city fell when troggs boiled up from below. High Tinker Mekkatorque flooded the halls with toxic radiation to stop them, poisoning many of his own people, while the traitor Thermaplugg seized the ruins.
Maraudon: Sacred to the centaur, these caverns hold the tomb of Zaetar, a son of Cenarius, whose union with the earth elemental princess Theradras birthed their race. Theradras still guards his remains in the depths.
Ragefire Chasm: A volcanic labyrinth running beneath Orgrimmar itself, Ragefire Chasm hides troggs and the Searing Blade cultists, who plot treachery against the Horde right under the Warchief's feet.
Razorfen Downs: These thorny warrens were once a quilboar holy site. Now the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer commands the place, turning the boar-folk into undead servants of the Scourge.
Razorfen Kraul: Colossal brambles sprouted where the demigod Agamaggan fell fighting the Burning Legion in ancient times. The quilboar revere these thorns as their birthplace and nest deep within them.
Ruins of Lordaeron: Once the proud capital of Lordaeron, this is where Prince Arthas came home a hero and murdered his father, King Terenas, on the throne. The broken city above now hides the Forsaken's Undercity.
Scarlet Monastery: A walled abbey in Tirisfal Glades serves as a bastion of the Scarlet Crusade, whose zealots see Scourge taint everywhere. Within, High Inquisitor Whitemane and Commander Mograine lead the faithful.
Scholomance: Beneath Caer Darrow, the Barov family's crypts became a school of necromancy for the Cult of the Damned after the Barovs traded their estate to Kel'Thuzad. Darkmaster Gandling oversees its ghastly lessons.
Shadowfang Keep: Archmage Arugal summoned the worgen to fight the Scourge, but they ran wild across Silverpine. From the old keep of Baron Silverlaine he now commands them, his sanity long since lost.
Stratholme: Arthas purged this plague-ridden city during the infamous Culling. Its burned streets are now fought over by Baron Rivendare's Scourge and a Scarlet Crusade led by a dreadlord in disguise.
Temple of Atal'Hakkar: Exiled Atal'ai priests raised this temple to summon Hakkar the Soulflayer, until Ysera, the Dreamer, sank it into the Swamp of Sorrows. Green dragons still keep watch over its drowned halls.
The Deadmines: Edwin VanCleef's Defias Brotherhood, stonemasons cheated of their pay by Stormwind's nobles, hide in the Moonbrook mines. There they quietly build a pirate juggernaut with which to strike back at the kingdom.
The Stockade: Stormwind's prison has fallen to a riot, with Defias thugs and other inmates seizing the cells. It is one of the few dungeons set entirely inside a capital city's walls.
Uldaman: A vault built by the titans and buried under the Badlands, Uldaman draws both the Explorers' League and Dark Iron diggers. Its records suggest the dwarves descend from the earthen, beings of living stone.
Wailing Caverns: The druid Naralex hoped to restore the Barrens through the Emerald Dream, but his dream became a nightmare. His Druids of the Fang turned twisted, and the caves came alive with monstrous beasts.
Zul'Farrak: The sun-baked citadel of the Sandfury trolls rises out of the Tanaris desert. Chief Ukorz Sandscalp rules here, and legend says the trolls can call the great hydra Gahz'rilla from its sacred pool.
Gurubashi Arena: A ring of ancient troll stone amid the ruins of the Gurubashi Empire, the arena is a lawless free-for-all. Every few hours a treasure chest drops into the pit, and only the last fighter standing claims it.
Blackwing Lair: At the summit of Blackrock Spire, Nefarian, son of Deathwing, works on his darkest project. He blends the blood of every dragonflight to breed chromatic dragons and an army worthy of his father.
Hyjal Summit: On these slopes the night elves, humans and orcs stood together against Archimonde at the end of the Third War. Malfurion Stormrage then unleashed the power of the World Tree, Nordrassil, to destroy the demon lord.
Molten Core: In the burning heart of Blackrock Mountain dwells Ragnaros the Firelord, bound to Azeroth since the Dark Irons summoned him centuries ago. His majordomo, Executus, commands the elemental host guarding him.
Naxxramas: A floating necropolis drifts above the Plaguelands, home to the lich Kel'Thuzad, the Lich King's most loyal lieutenant. From its four quarters, abominations, spiders and death knights prepare the Scourge's next blow.
Onyxia's Lair: In a cave in Dustwallow Marsh lies the lair of Onyxia, Deathwing's daughter. In human form as Lady Katrana Prestor, she whispers poisoned counsel into the ears of Stormwind's nobles.
Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj: Once the Scarab Gong was struck, the Scarab Wall opened onto the outer ruins of the qiraji empire. Ossirian the Unscarred commands the insectoid host that the Cenarion Circle hopes to stop.
Temple of Ahn'Qiraj: Deep within the qiraji temple-city, the Twin Emperors and their silithid swarms serve a far older master: C'Thun, an imprisoned Old God whose whispers stir the desert.
Zul'Gurub: The ancient capital of the Gurubashi trolls lies hidden in the Stranglethorn jungle. Its Hakkari priests have summoned Hakkar the Soulflayer, the god of blood, back into the world.
Aerie Peak: The Wildhammer dwarves keep their gryphon roosts on this craggy height in the Hinterlands. Their famed riders are led by Falstad Wildhammer, and they distrust their stuffier Bronzebeard cousins.
Astranaar: This night elf town stands on an island in an Ashenvale lake. Its Sentinels watch the forest's edges, where Warsong orcs fell the ancient trees to build the Horde's new towns.
Auberdine: This quiet night elf harbour on the Darkshore coast is the Alliance's main link between the continents. Ships sail from here to Teldrassil's roots and to Menethil Harbor.
Bloodvenom Post: A hardy Horde camp in corrupted Felwood, named for the tainted Bloodvenom river nearby. The demons of the Burning Legion poisoned this once-lovely forest during the Third War.
Booty Bay: This goblin port of the Steamwheedle Cartel is built into the cliffs around a hidden cove, and you enter through the jaws of a giant shark skull. Baron Revilgaz keeps it neutral, at least for paying customers.
Brackenwall Village: A rough Horde settlement deep in the reeds of Dustwallow Marsh. From here the Horde keeps a close eye on Jaina Proudmoore's Theramore and on the black dragons that haunt the swamp.
Camp Mojache: This tauren camp of painted hide tents gives the Horde a foothold in the green wilds of Feralas, close to the haunted ruins of Dire Maul.
Camp Taurajo: This large tauren camp guards the southern Barrens. It sits on the crossroads that lead to Mulgore and down to the mesas of Thousand Needles.
Cenarion Hold: The Cenarion Circle built this desert stronghold to watch the Qiraji behind the Scarab Wall. Druids, scouts and the bronze dragonflight's allies gather here as the swarm's return draws near.
Chillwind Camp: This Alliance encampment is a cold, foggy foothold at the edge of the Western Plaguelands. From here adventurers strike at the Scourge and at the necromancers of Scholomance.
Crossroads: Thrall's orcs built this fortified waystation where the main roads of the Barrens meet. Its wooden palisade is often tested by raiding centaur and quilboar, yet the caravans keep moving.
Darkshire: The last true town in gloomy Duskwood is guarded by the Night Watch against worgen, ghouls and the restless dead of Raven Hill. Its folk hold on stubbornly under endless twilight.
Everlook: This goblin trading town lies among the snowy peaks of Winterspring and welcomes Horde and Alliance alike, provided their coin is good. Its bruisers keep the peace with blunt efficiency.
Feathermoon: Feathermoon Stronghold is a night elf fortress on an island off the Feralas coast. Its Sentinels guard the Alliance's hold on the region and keep a wary eye on the Highborne ruins inland.
Flame Crest: This rugged Horde camp sits on the ash-choked hills of the Burning Steppes. From here orcs loyal to Thrall watch Blackrock Mountain and the renegade Dark Horde within it.
Freewind Post: This tauren village perches atop a sheer stone pillar in Thousand Needles. Visitors reach it by lift, and its huts are linked to neighbouring mesas by swaying rope bridges.
Grom'gol Base Camp: This Horde camp in the Stranglethorn jungle is named for Grom Hellscream. Its zeppelin tower links this humid frontier to Orgrimmar and the Undercity, far across the sea.
Hammerfall: This was once an internment camp where defeated orcs were held. The Horde named it for Orgrim Doomhammer, who fell when Thrall's forces freed the prisoners, and later reclaimed it as a stronghold.
Kargath: A Horde fortress dug into the canyons of the Badlands, named for Kargath Bladefist, the Shattered Hand chieftain who lost a hand of his own. Its grunts watch the Dark Iron dwarves and the Uldaman dig.
Lakeshire: A peaceful-looking human village on Lake Everstill in Redridge. Blackrock orcs and gnoll raiders press on it from the hills, and its bridge seems forever under repair.
Light's Hope Chapel: The Argent Dawn's chapel stands on hallowed ground deep in the Eastern Plaguelands. It is a lone beacon against the Scourge, and the place where the war on Naxxramas is planned.
Marshal's Refuge: This neutral camp hides in a cave under the rim of Un'Goro Crater, where explorers and naturalists shelter from devilsaurs and study the crater's strange glowing crystals.
Menethil Harbor: This Alliance port in the soggy Wetlands bears the name of Lordaeron's royal house. It ships travellers across the sea, while Dragonmaw orcs still lurk in the hills near Grim Batol.
Morgan's Vigil: This Alliance outpost guards the pass between the Burning Steppes and Redridge. From here the Alliance fights back against the Blackrock orcs who spill from Blackrock Mountain.
Nethergarde Keep: This fortress, manned with the help of Kirin Tor mages, stands watch over the Blasted Lands and the dormant Dark Portal. It is ready should demons or orcs ever come through again.
Nighthaven: This druid sanctuary in Moonglade lies on the shores of Lake Elune'ara and is overseen by Keeper Remulos. Druids of every race gather here in peace, whatever their allegiance.
Nijel's Point: Alliance travellers find a rare green refuge here on a ridge above the grey wastes of Desolace, which the warring centaur clans have made a dangerous place to cross.
Ratchet: The bustling goblin port on the Barrens coast is run by the Steamwheedle Cartel. Its boats sail to Booty Bay, and its docks welcome anyone with something to sell.
Refuge Pointe: This Alliance camp in the Arathi Highlands shelters the survivors and loyalists of fallen Stromgarde. They still dream of retaking their kingdom from ogres, trolls and the Syndicate.
Revantusk Village: This seaside village belongs to the Revantusk tribe of forest trolls, who have sided with the Horde. They fight their cruel Vilebranch cousins and the Wildhammer dwarves of the Hinterlands.
Rut'theran Village: This small night elf village sits among the roots of Teldrassil, where ships from Darkshore come ashore. A glowing portal carries visitors up into Darnassus.
Sentinel Hill: Gryan Stoutmantle's People's Militia holds this tower in Westfall. Abandoned by Stormwind, the farmers here have taken up arms against the Defias Brotherhood and its masked raiders.
Shadowprey Village: This Horde village stands on the rocky western shore of Desolace. It gives tauren and trolls a base from which to deal with the warring centaur clans inland.
Southshore: This Alliance fishing town in the Hillsbrad Foothills is locked in an endless feud with the Forsaken of Tarren Mill. Nearby stands Durnholde Keep, where young Thrall was raised as a slave.
Splintertree Post: This Warsong outpost sits on Ashenvale's eastern edge. Its orc lumberjacks cut timber for the Horde under the constant threat of night elf Sentinel raids.
Steamwheedle Port: This goblin dock on the Tanaris coast is run by the Steamwheedle Cartel. It is a salty trading post where neutrality is good for business and pirates are bad for it.
Stonard: This walled orcish fortress is the Horde's stronghold in the Swamp of Sorrows. It is a grim outpost set amid the reeds, not far from the sunken temple of the Atal'ai.
Stonetalon Peak: This night elf outpost stands high on the slopes of the Stonetalon Mountains. Its keepers watch helplessly as the Venture Company's machines tear into the old forests below.
Stormwind Harbor: The busy waterfront of the human capital is where ships of Stormwind's fleet and merchant vessels tie up. Through it pass the troops and trade that bind the kingdom to distant shores.
Sun Rock Retreat: This tauren refuge is cut into a high ridge in the Stonetalon Mountains. It is a peaceful lookout over lands scarred by the Venture Company's greed.
Talonbranch Glade: This night elf outpost lies in northern Felwood. Here the Alliance and the guardians of nature work to hold back the demonic corruption that has poisoned the forest.
Talrendis Point: This night elf outpost lies on the edge of Azshara, among the ruins of the Highborne. Its Sentinels guard the forest against the orcs of nearby Valormok.
Tarren Mill: Once a human farming village, Tarren Mill is now a Forsaken stronghold. Its apothecaries brew foul things and its soldiers trade blows endlessly with Southshore down the road.
Thalanaar: This night elf outpost guards the road where the forests of Feralas meet the canyons of Thousand Needles. Moonwell water flows here, and Sentinels watch over travellers.
The Sepulcher: The Forsaken set up this base in an old crypt in Silverpine Forest. From here they fight worgen, Scourge stragglers and Arugal's forces at Shadowfang Keep.
Thelsamar: This sturdy dwarven town lies on the road through Loch Modan, where the Mountaineers hold the line against troggs and Dark Iron saboteurs. It sits not far from the great Stonewrought Dam.
Theramore Isle: Jaina Proudmoore led the survivors of Lordaeron across the sea to found this island city in Dustwallow Marsh. Its harbour is the Alliance's greatest stronghold on Kalimdor.
Thorium Point: This is the outpost of the Thorium Brotherhood, master smiths who broke away from the Dark Iron dwarves. From here they trade their secrets with any adventurer who earns their respect.
Valormok: This Horde camp lies on the edge of Azshara, among the haunted ruins of the night elves' ancient queen. The Horde holds it in defiance of the Sentinels nearby.
Zoram'gar Outpost: This Horde camp sits on the Zoram Strand coast of Ashenvale, near the sunken temple of Blackfathom Deeps. From here orcs and trolls scout the naga and the night elves alike.
Alterac Mountains: These frozen peaks once held the human kingdom of Alterac. Its king, Aiden Perenolde, betrayed the Alliance to the Horde in the Second War, and today the Syndicate and ogres prowl its ruins.
Arathi Highlands: This was the seat of Arathor, the first human empire, founded by Thoradin. The ruins of Stromgarde and the old internment camps still dot its rolling, contested hills.
Ashenvale: This ancient, twilit forest has belonged to the night elves for millennia. Here Grom Hellscream slew the demigod Cenarius, and Horde lumber camps and Sentinels still clash under its trees.
Azshara: This haunted coast bears the name of the night elves' last queen, whose Highborne summoned the Burning Legion. Their ruined palaces and statues still look out over the sea.
Badlands: This sun-blasted waste of red rock and dry canyons was once a fertile land. Ogres, Dark Iron dwarves and black dragons now roam it, and the titan vault of Uldaman lies buried beneath.
Blasted Lands: This land was the Black Morass before the orcs opened the Dark Portal. That magic left it a scorched, demon-haunted ruin, now guarded by the Alliance's Nethergarde Keep.
Burning Steppes: When the Dark Iron dwarves summoned Ragnaros in the War of the Three Hammers, his fiery arrival burned this land to cinders. Blackrock Mountain still smoulders over its blackened plains.
Darkshore: This misty night elf coastline is scattered with ancient ruins and haunted barrow dens. Its quiet harbour at Auberdine links the island of Teldrassil to the wider world.
Deadwind Pass: A barren valley where nothing seems to grow, Deadwind Pass hides Karazhan, the dark tower of the last Guardian, Medivh. Since his fall its halls have been home only to ghosts.
Desolace: This grey, lifeless land is torn by the feuding centaur clans, the children of Zaetar and Theradras. Their sacred caverns of Maraudon lie at its heart.
Dun Morogh: These snowy peaks are the homeland of the dwarves and gnomes, home to Ironforge and the ruined city of Gnomeregan. Many young adventurers take their first steps in its frosty valleys.
Durotar: Thrall named this harsh red land after his father, Durotan, chieftain of the Frostwolves, and built the new orcish homeland here. Darkspear trolls share its shores at Sen'jin Village.
Duskwood: This forest lies in near-permanent twilight. Worgen prowl its woods, the dead walk at Raven Hill, and the Night Watch of Darkshire struggles to keep the darkness at bay.
Dustwallow Marsh: This fog-bound swamp holds both Jaina Proudmoore's Theramore and the lair of the black dragon Onyxia. Its mists hide deserters, ogres and the restless dead.
Eastern Plaguelands: This is the heartland of the Scourge's conquest, where the plague turned rich farmland into rot. Stratholme smoulders here, and the Argent Dawn holds out at Light's Hope Chapel.
Elwynn Forest: This green, golden forest is the heart of the Kingdom of Stormwind. It is home to Northshire Abbey, the inn at Goldshire, and the farms that feed the capital.
Felwood: This was once a lush night elf forest, until the Burning Legion's demons poisoned it in the Third War. Now its trees are twisted, its waters tainted, and satyrs roam freely.
Feralas: This wild, rain-soaked jungle holds giant trees and ancient Highborne ruins, among them the vast halls of Dire Maul. Ogres, hippogryphs and yetis roam its overgrown valleys.
Hillsbrad Foothills: Young Thrall grew up here as a gladiator slave at Durnholde Keep. Now the green hills are a battleground where Southshore and Tarren Mill wage an endless feud.
Loch Modan: This pastoral dwarven valley is built around the Stonewrought Dam, which holds back the loch's waters. The Mountaineers of Thelsamar keep the troggs and Dark Irons in check.
Moonglade: This sacred glade is the home of the Cenarion Circle and their druids, watched over by Keeper Remulos. Druids of all races meet here, and all fighting is set aside.
Mount Hyjal: The great World Tree Nordrassil rises from this mountain, the site of the final battle of the Third War. There Archimonde fell, and the night elves gave up their immortality to stop him.
Mulgore: These rolling golden plains are the ancestral homeland of the tauren. Herds of kodo and plainstriders graze below the mesas of Thunder Bluff, and the tauren hunt them with deep reverence for the Earth Mother.
Redridge Mountains: These red hills circle Lake Everstill and its town of Lakeshire. Blackrock orcs and gnoll war bands raid them constantly, and Stormwind seems slow to send help.
Searing Gorge: This scorched pit is scarred by Dark Iron mining near Blackrock Mountain. The Thorium Brotherhood holds out here among the slag, cinders and fire elementals.
Shen'dralas: The Shen'dralas are Highborne who stayed sealed within Eldre'Thalas, today's Dire Maul, after the Sundering. They kept their magic alive by draining a bound demon, Immol'thar, under Prince Tortheldrin.
Silithus: This blistering desert hides the hive-city of Ahn'Qiraj behind the ancient Scarab Wall. The Cenarion Circle watches it nervously, while Twilight's Hammer cultists gather at strange stone circles.
Silverpine Forest: This dark pine woodland stretches along the coast south of Tirisfal. Archmage Arugal's worgen haunt Shadowfang Keep, and a curse turns the villagers of Pyrewood into beasts at night.
Stonetalon Mountains: These high peaks hold ancient groves sacred to the druids. The Venture Company has stripped and burned whole valleys of them in its hunt for timber and profit.
Stranglethorn Vale: This sweltering jungle holds the ruins of the old Gurubashi troll empire, including Zul'Gurub. Big-game hunters, pirates and goblin traders all try to carve out a share of it.
Swamp of Sorrows: This misty, mournful bog hides the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar beneath its waters. The Horde holds the grim fortress of Stonard here, amid the stagnant pools and the reeds.
Tanaris: This vast desert is home to the goblin town of Gadgetzan and the troll city of Zul'Farrak. Somewhere among its dunes lie the Caverns of Time, guarded by the bronze dragonflight.
Teldrassil: This colossal World Tree was planted by Archdruid Fandral Staghelm off Kalimdor's northern coast without the dragon Aspects' blessing. The night elf capital, Darnassus, lies in its branches.
The Barrens: This vast, sunbaked savanna lies at the heart of Kalimdor. It is dotted with quilboar thorns, centaur camps and the Wailing Caverns, while the Horde's Crossroads keeps watch at its centre.
The Hinterlands: These rugged forested highlands are home to the Wildhammer gryphon riders of Aerie Peak, the troll ruins of the Vilebranch, and the Revantusk tribe, who are allied with the Horde.
Thousand Needles: This canyon of towering stone spires is home to tauren mesa villages, centaur raiders, and the Shimmering Flats, where gnomes and goblins race their contraptions across the dry lakebed.
Tirisfal Glades: This misty, shadowed region is home to the Forsaken, risen from the ruins of Lordaeron's heartland. The Scarlet Crusade still holds a monastery on its northern edge.
Un'Goro Crater: This steaming jungle crater looks like a lost world, full of dinosaurs and strange crystals. Lore holds that it was a titan workshop, where life itself was tested and shaped.
Western Plaguelands: This was Lordaeron's breadbasket until the Cult of the Damned spread the plague through its grain at Andorhal. Necromancers now gather at Scholomance on the isle of Caer Darrow.
Westfall: This farmland once fed Stormwind, until the Defias Brotherhood rose in revolt. Now its fields lie abandoned to harvest golems, and only Sentinel Hill keeps up the fight.
Wetlands: This rain-soaked marsh links Khaz Modan to the north across the Thandol Span. Dragonmaw orcs still hold Grim Batol here, along with the red dragons they once enslaved.
Winterspring: This snowbound valley in northern Kalimdor holds frostsabers, furbolgs and the goblin trading town of Everlook. Old night elf ruins lie hidden under its drifts.
